newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets rise.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of August 30 were $3.701 billion, compared with $3.529 billion on August 23.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of August 30 were $15.444 billion, compared with $15.387 billion as of August 23.
It said the increase in international assets was due to:
- Revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of 169 million
- Other foreign exchange revenues worth a net $13 million.
- A net sale of currency to the federal government for $10 million to cover debt servicing charges.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base rose 1.545 billion pesos due to seasonal demand for notes and coins stemming from salary payments for the second two weeks of August.
Central bank credit to banks rose 2.724 billion pesos to meet the rising demand for notes and coins.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
